verses.text: Brothers and sisters, you know our visit to you wasn't wasted.
Even after we had suffered and been mistreated in Philippi, as you know, we found courage in God to share his Good News with you despite strong opposition.
Our appeal didn't come from error, impure motives, or trickery.
Instead, God approved us and entrusted us with the Good News. So we speak to please God, who examines our hearts, not to please people.
As you know, we never used flattery or put on a show to cover greed. God is our witness.
We weren't looking for praise from people—not from you or anyone else—even though as Christ's apostles we could have made demands.
Instead, we were gentle among you, like a nursing mother tenderly caring for her own children.
We cared for you so deeply that we were glad to share with you not only God's Good News but our own lives too. You had become dear to us.
Brothers and sisters, you remember our hard work. We worked night and day so we wouldn't burden anyone while we shared God's Good News with you.
You and God are witnesses of how holy, just, and blameless we were toward you who believe.
You know how we encouraged, comforted, and urged each one of you, like a father with his children,
to live in a way worthy of God, who calls you into his own Kingdom and glory.
We also thank God constantly because when you received God's message from us, you welcomed it for what it truly is—not a human message but God's word, which is at work in you who believe.
Brothers and sisters, you became imitators of God's churches in Judea in Christ Jesus. You suffered the same things from your own people as they did from the Judeans,
who killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets, drove us out, and displease God by opposing everyone.
They try to stop us from speaking to the Gentiles so they might be saved. In this way they keep piling up their sins. But God's anger has finally come upon them.
Brothers and sisters, when we were separated from you for a short time in person—but never in heart—we tried all the harder, with great longing, to see you face to face.
We wanted to come to you. I, Paul, tried again and again, but Satan blocked our way.
After all, what is our hope, joy, or crown to celebrate? Isn't it you, standing before our Lord Jesus when he comes?
You are our glory and joy.
